body:
## Problem

Incorrect usage documentation. `README.md:29-35` says the generated `eslint.config.mjs` contains `{ "extends": ["@ivuorinen"] }`, and `README.md:39-47` tells Jest users to use `{ "extends": ["@ivuorinen/eslint-config/jest"] }`. Both are legacy eslintrc syntax. The package exports flat-config arrays (`index.cjs`, `jest.cjs`), depends on ESLint 10, and ESLint 10 no longer reads eslintrc files at all.

## Evidence

The postinstall actually writes a flat config (`scripts/postinstall.cjs`): `import ivuorinenConfig from '@ivuorinen/eslint-config'; export default [...ivuorinenConfig, …]`.

Consumer reproduction (npm 11.19, ESLint 10.11.0, project with the README's Jest snippet in `.eslintrc.json` and no flat config):

```text
$ npx eslint b.test.js
Oops! Something went wrong! :(
ESLint: 10.11.0
exit 2
```

## Impact

A user following the only documented way to enable the Jest rules gets a crashing ESLint; the generated-file description also misleads anyone writing the config by hand (e.g. every Yarn 4 user, whose postinstall never runs).

## Fix

Replace both JSON blocks with flat-config examples:

```js
// eslint.config.mjs
import ivuorinen from '@ivuorinen/eslint-config'
import ivuorinenJest from '@ivuorinen/eslint-config/jest'

export default [
  ...ivuorinen,
  ...ivuorinenJest.map(config => ({ ...config, files: ['**/*.test.{js,mjs,cjs}'] })),
]
```

and state that ESLint 10 flat config is required (no `.eslintrc*` support).

## Resolution
README Installation and Jest sections rewritten to flat-config examples (eslint.config.mjs), stating ESLint 10 reads no .eslintrc. Verified in a scratch consumer (npm pack + npm install): the README's `[...ivuorinenConfig, ...ivuorinenJest]` config lints — jest/no-disabled-tests fires on src/a.test.js, src/app.js parses.
title: README documents eslintrc JSON that ESLint 10 cannot load; the package is flat-config only

body:
## Problem

`index.cjs:36-38` sets `languageOptions.parserOptions.ecmaVersion: 12` (ES2021) for `**/*.{js,mjs,cjs}`. Any consumer file that uses syntax newer than ES2021 fails to parse, so ESLint reports a single fatal "Parsing error" for the file and applies no rules to it at all.

## Evidence

Verified with ESLint 10.2.0 `Linter.verify(code, require('./index.cjs'), 'src/x.mjs')`:

```text
ES2022 class private field   PARSE ERROR: Parsing error: Unexpected character '#'
ES2022 top-level await       PARSE ERROR: Parsing error: Cannot use keyword 'await' outside an async function
ES2021 logical assign        ok
ES2024 regex v flag          PARSE ERROR: Parsing error: Invalid regular expression flag
```

The `engines` field targets Node 20+, where all three are ordinary syntax. `tests/index.test.js` only lints ES2015-era snippets, so the suite passes.

## Impact

Consumers writing current JavaScript (private class fields, top-level await in `.mjs`) get red lint runs on valid code; worse, every such file is excluded from linting entirely because rules never run after a fatal parse error.

## Fix

Delete the `parserOptions: { ecmaVersion: 12 }` block (ESLint's flat-config default is `ecmaVersion: "latest"`), or set `languageOptions: { ecmaVersion: "latest", sourceType: … }` explicitly. Add a regression case to `tests/index.test.js` that lints `class A { #x = 1 }` and a top-level `await` and asserts no fatal message.

## Resolution
Removed parserOptions.ecmaVersion: 12 from index.cjs (flat-config default is latest). New tests/syntax.test.js asserts zero fatal messages for class private fields, top-level await and the regex v flag; it failed with 'Parsing error' before the fix (observed RED) and passes after.
title: ecmaVersion 12 makes every ES2022+ consumer file a fatal parsing error

body:
## Problem

Unused production dependency. `package.json:64` declares `"typescript": ">=4.2.0"` in `dependencies`. No code in the package uses it, the range floats across every future major, and it installs the TypeScript 7 toolchain — including the prebuilt Go `tsc` binary — into every consumer project.

## Evidence

Manifest: `package.json:64` (`dependencies`). Lockfile: `typescript@npm:>=4.2.0` → 7.0.2, plus `@typescript/typescript-linux-x64` 7.0.2 and 19 other platform binaries. Usage scan (every import form): no `require`/`import` of `typescript` in `index.cjs`, `jest.cjs`, the wrappers or `scripts/`; no `tsc` in scripts. The only loader in the runtime tree is `eslint-plugin-n/lib/util/get-full-type-name.js`, which wraps `require("typescript")` in `try { … } catch { return null }`. With `typescript` blocked from resolution, `Linter.verify` on `index.cjs` returns 0 fatal messages. `eslint-plugin-jest` declares `typescript` as an optional peer `>=4.8.4 <7.0.0`, which the resolved 7.0.2 violates.

Downstream: `base-configs-stylelint`'s open `security-2a247550` traces GO-2026-5970 (golang.org/x/text 0.38.0 inside that Go binary) to exactly this dependency.

## Impact

Every consumer downloads and stores a compiler and native binary they never use, inherits its vulnerability reports (GO-2026-5970 today), and is exposed to whatever TypeScript major ships next.

## Fix

Remove `typescript` from `dependencies` (approve per dependency — a consumer that relied on it transitively for its own `tsc` would need to declare it). If type-aware `eslint-plugin-n` or `eslint-plugin-jest` rules are ever enabled, declare it as an optional `peerDependency` with a bounded range (e.g. `">=4.8.4 <7.0.0"`) instead.

## Resolution
Removed "typescript": ">=4.2.0" from dependencies (owner-approved). yarn.lock now has 0 typescript and 0 @typescript/typescript-* entries; the packed package.json has no typescript. 25/25 tests and self-lint pass. Note: npm consumers still get typescript 6.0.3 auto-installed as a peer of eslint-plugin-n / @typescript-eslint (third-party), but no longer TypeScript 7 or its Go binary.
title: typescript is an unused production dependency that installs TypeScript 7 in every consumer

body:
## Problem

Declared-surface drift. `package.json:12-14` declares `"node": "^20.9.0 || >=21.1.0"` (ESLint 9's range). The runtime dependencies now require ESLint 10's range, which excludes Node 20.9-20.18, all of 21, 22.0-22.12 and 23.

## Evidence

Fresh install of the committed lockfile; `semver.satisfies` against every package in the `dependencies` closure (193 packages):

```text
node 22.12.0 blocked by: @eslint/js 10.0.1 (^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24); eslint 10.2.0 (same); eslint-config-eslint 14.0.0 (same); @eslint/config-array 0.23.4 (same)
versions satisfying the closure: 20.19.0, 20.20.2, 22.13.0, 22.14.0, 22.19.0, 22.22.2, 24.x, 26.0.0
```

## Impact

Consumers on Node 21, 23, 20.9-20.18 or 22.0-22.12 are told they are supported, install without a hard error, and run an ESLint that does not support their runtime.

## Fix

Set `"engines": { "node": "^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24" }` and note the floor change in the next release notes.

## Resolution
Owner chose (s)pec: engines.node set to "^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24", ESLint 10's own range.
title: engines promises Node ^20.9.0 || >=21.1.0 but ESLint 10 needs ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24

body:
## Problem

The package ships `"postinstall": "node scripts/postinstall.cjs"`. pnpm 12 fails the install with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` for any dependency with an unapproved build script; Yarn 4 defaults to `enableScripts: false` and skips it. `README.md:29` promises "After installing it, a _`eslint.config.mjs`_ file will be created automatically".

## Evidence

Consumer installs in scratch projects (pnpm 12.4.1, Yarn 4.18.0, npm 11.19.0):

```text
$ pnpm add -D @ivuorinen/base-configs     # includes this package
ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS: … @ivuorinen/eslint-config 1.5.17 …  → exit 1
$ CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile  # config package present
ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS → exit 1
$ pnpm add -D prettier                    # control, no build script → exit 0
Yarn 4: YN0004 … all build scripts have been disabled → exit 0, no eslint.config.mjs written
```

npm 11.19 still runs it but warns `install-scripts not yet covered by allowScripts`.

## Impact

pnpm 12 consumers cannot install; Yarn 4 consumers get no `eslint.config.mjs`, and ESLint 10 then refuses to run without a config — the user is left to write one from the README, whose examples are the broken eslintrc JSON.

## Fix

Replace the `postinstall` with an explicit initializer `bin` (e.g. `npx eslint-config-init` running today's script) and document the flat-config file to create by hand. If the postinstall stays, document the pnpm (`pnpm approve-builds`) and Yarn 4 behaviour in the README.

## Resolution
Owner chose the document-only fix: README now states npm runs the postinstall (with an allowScripts warning), Yarn 4 does not, and pnpm fails until the package is approved (pnpm approve-builds / onlyBuiltDependencies), and gives the file to create by hand. The postinstall itself is unchanged by owner decision.
title: postinstall breaks pnpm 12 installs and never runs under Yarn 4, contrary to the README

## Problem

Dependency vulnerability. `yarn.lock` resolves `nanoid` 3.3.16, affected by GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 / CVE-2026-67213 (High, fixed in 3.3.18).

## Evidence

osv-scanner 2.6.0 (`GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8`, HIGH) and `yarn npm audit --all --recursive` (advisory 1139427, `high`, `vulnerable: <3.3.18`, tree 3.3.16) agree.

## Impact

Vulnerable ID generator in the dev/test toolchain (vitest's dependency tree).

## Fix

`yarn up -R nanoid` (or `resolutions: { "nanoid": "^3.3.18" }` if the parent range caps it), `yarn install`, re-scan with osv-scanner.

## Resolution
yarn up -R nanoid pacote: nanoid now 3.3.19. osv-scanner scan source --lockfile=yarn.lock: No issues found.
title: nanoid 3.3.16 is vulnerable to GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 (High)

body:
## Problem

`jest.cjs:10-17` scopes the Jest globals to `files: ["**/*.{js,mjs,cjs}"]` and then spreads `flat/recommended` and `flat/style`, which carry no `files` at all. Spread as documented, the Jest environment covers production source: `describe`/`expect`/`test` become defined globals everywhere and Jest rules fire on non-test files. The third object (lines 20-27) re-adds `flat/recommended`'s rules and the plugin, duplicating element 2.

## Evidence

ESLint 10.2.0 `Linter.verify` of `describe("x", () => {})\nexpect(1)\ntest.skip("a", () => {})` as `src/app.js` with `[{ settings: { jest: { version: 29 } } }, ...index, ...jest]`:

```text
no-undef on src/app.js: 0          (base config alone: 2)
jest rules on src/app.js: jest/valid-expect, jest/no-disabled-tests, jest/expect-expect
jestCfg[1].files: undefined
obj3 duplicates recommended rules: true
```

## Impact

A stray `describe(`/`expect(` left in production code is no longer caught by `no-undef`, and Jest style rules produce noise on ordinary modules. Consumers cannot tell from the README that they must wrap the config in their own `files` block.

## Fix

Scope every element to test files and drop the duplicate:

```js
const files = ['**/*.{test,spec}.{js,mjs,cjs}', '**/__tests__/**/*.{js,mjs,cjs}']
module.exports = [
  { files, languageOptions: { globals: { ...jest.globals } } },
  { files, ...jest.configs['flat/recommended'] },
  { files, ...jest.configs['flat/style'] },
]
```

and add a test asserting no `jest/*` rule fires on `src/app.js`.

## Resolution
jest.cjs: every element scoped to **/*.{test,spec}.{js,mjs,cjs} and **/__tests__/**; duplicate third object removed. New cases in tests/jest.test.js (no jest/* rule and 2 no-undef hits on src/app.js) failed before (observed RED) and pass after; the original rule tests on my.test.js still pass.
title: The jest config applies Jest globals and rules to every JS file, not just tests

body:
## Problem

Coverage hole. `tests/index.test.js:2` and `tests/jest.test.js:2` import `../index.cjs` / `../jest.cjs` by relative path, so the published `exports` map (`.` and `./jest`, both conditions) is never exercised; and every `describeRules` case uses ES2015-era code, so no test fails when the config cannot parse current syntax.

## Evidence

Mutation check against the real defect: `index.cjs` sets `ecmaVersion: 12`, which makes `class A { #x = 1 }` a fatal parse error (see the correctness finding) — `yarn test` still reports `Tests 16 passed (16)`. The sibling `base-configs-commitlint/test/resolve.test.mjs` resolves the package by its own name for exactly this reason ("A broken entry — e.g. exports.require pointing at a missing file — fails here exactly as a real consumer would experience it"), and `base-configs-stylelint`'s shipped `./css` exports bug is the precedent for what such a test catches.

## Impact

The two ways this package can break every consumer — an unresolvable entry point and a parser setting that rejects valid code — are both invisible to the suite that gates publishing.

## Fix

Add `tests/exports.test.js` that imports `@ivuorinen/eslint-config` and `@ivuorinen/eslint-config/jest` by name (ESM) and via `createRequire` (CJS) and asserts both are non-empty arrays; add `describeRules`-style cases asserting zero fatal messages for `class A { #x = 1 }`, a top-level `await` in `.mjs`, and `/[\p{L}]/v`.

## Resolution
Added tests/syntax.test.js (modern syntax parses) and tests/exports.test.js (both published specifiers resolve by name via require and import). Failing-capability proven: syntax tests failed against the old config; pointing exports['./jest'].import at a missing file made the exports test fail (restored after).
title: Tests bypass the exports map and never lint modern syntax, so the parse-breaking config passes

body:
## Problem

Excess secret exposure. `publish.yml:15-16` and `pr-lint.yml:15-17` put `NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}` in the workflow-level `env:`, so every job and step receives it: the `Linter` job's MegaLinter action in `publish.yml`, and in `pr-lint.yml` the checkout, the corepack install and `Simek/yarn-lock-changes` (which is also handed it explicitly at line 48). Only the Semantic Release step needs an npm credential, and it could use none: the job already has `id-token: write` for OIDC trusted publishing, which `.github/zizmor.yml` notes is "tracked separately" while setup-node runs with `always-auth: true`.

## Evidence

semgrep and opengrep (`gha-workflow-env-secret`, WARNING) report `pr-lint.yml:16` and `publish.yml:16`; manual sweep confirms both and the explicit pass-through at `pr-lint.yml:47-48`. The sibling `base-configs-stylelint/.github/workflows/publish.yml:15-17` documents the fix: "NPM_TOKEN is deliberately NOT set at workflow level: that would put the publish credential in the environment of the lint and test jobs".

## Impact

A compromised lint action or any tool MegaLinter runs can read a token that can publish `@ivuorinen/eslint-config`; on `pull_request` the exposure recurs on every same-repo PR, including every Renovate/Dependabot branch.

## Fix

Delete both workflow-level `env:` blocks and the `NPM_TOKEN` lines on the lint steps; set `NPM_TOKEN` only on the Semantic Release step. Better: finish the move to trusted publishing (configure the npm trusted publisher, drop `always-auth` and `NPM_TOKEN` entirely, as `base-configs-semantic-release` did) and delete the secret.

## Resolution
Removed the workflow-level env blocks from publish.yml and pr-lint.yml and the NPM_TOKEN lines on both lint steps; NPM_TOKEN now appears only on the Semantic Release step. Moving to OIDC trusted publishing (registry-side setup, secret deletion) remains the owner's action.
title: NPM_TOKEN is exposed workflow-wide in publish.yml and pr-lint.yml, including to third-party actions

body:
## Problem

Ad-hoc unpinned package. `publish.yml:66-68`, `test.yml:38-40` and `pr-lint.yml:38-40` run `npm install -g corepack --force && corepack enable`: whatever `corepack` version npm serves at that moment, with lifecycle scripts enabled. In `publish.yml` this runs inside the job holding `NPM_TOKEN`, `secrets.PAT` and `id-token: write`. `.github/zizmor.yml` suppresses the `adhoc-packages` audit for all three files.

## Evidence

```yaml
# .github/workflows/publish.yml:66-68
      - name: Install and enable corepack
        shell: sh
        run: npm install -g corepack --force && corepack enable
```

The sibling `base-configs-stylelint` pins the same step to a fixed version with `--ignore-scripts` ("Version pinned so the toolchain is reproducible, and --ignore-scripts so nothing in the install tree executes"), and `base-configs-commitlint` only installs a pinned copy on Node 25+.

## Impact

A malicious or broken corepack release executes with release credentials in scope and determines which Yarn binary builds the release; the zizmor suppression hides it from the linter that would flag it.

## Fix

Pin and disable scripts in all three files: `npm install -g --ignore-scripts corepack@0.35.0 && corepack enable` (or, on the Node 24 `.nvmrc`, just `corepack enable`, since Node 24 bundles corepack). Keep the zizmor ignore only with that justification.

## Resolution
publish.yml and test.yml now run `corepack enable` (Node 24 from .nvmrc bundles it); pr-lint.yml (no setup-node) installs a pinned corepack with --ignore-scripts only on Node 25+. zizmor.yml adhoc-packages ignore narrowed to pr-lint.yml. actionlint clean.
title: Release, test and lint jobs npm-install a floating corepack with install scripts enabled

body:
## Problem

`publish.yml:70-80` restores `node_modules` with `key: node-modules-${{ hashFiles('**/yarn.lock') }}` and runs `yarn install` only when the cache misses, without `--immutable`. A `package.json`-only change or a `.nvmrc` bump keeps the key, so the release runs on a stale tree; when the install does run, a manifest/lockfile mismatch is re-resolved instead of failing.

## Evidence

```yaml
          key: node-modules-${{ hashFiles('**/yarn.lock') }}
      - name: Install Dependencies
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: yarn install
```

`base-configs-stylelint/.github/workflows/publish.yml:86-93` records that this pattern already shipped a wrong release there (1.4.0 cut as a minor from stale `@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` rules).

## Impact

semantic-release reads its rules from `node_modules`; a stale tree can publish the wrong version bump.

## Fix

Run `yarn install --immutable --mode=skip-build` unconditionally (keep the cache as a speed-up) and add `.nvmrc` to the cache key.

## Resolution
publish.yml install now runs unconditionally as `yarn install --immutable --mode=skip-build`; cache key includes .nvmrc.
title: Release install is skipped on a cache hit keyed only on yarn.lock and is not --immutable

body:
## Problem

`.github/renovate.json` lacks the `packageRules` entry `base-configs-semantic-release` and `base-configs-stylelint` use to give GitHub Actions and pre-commit updates the `actions` scope; a major action bump becomes `chore(deps)!: …`, which the shared release rules map to `major`.

## Evidence

This repo's `v1.0.0` came from commits including `0571d0e chore(deps)!: update actions/checkout (v5.0.1 → v6.0.0) (#69)`, `56ba11e chore(deps)!: update github/codeql-action (v3.30.6 → v4.30.7) (#45)` and `cc95eb3 chore(deps)!: update renovatebot/pre-commit-hooks (41.159.4 → 42.0.0) (#61)`.

## Impact

The next major action or hook bump publishes a new major of `@ivuorinen/eslint-config` with no consumer-visible change.

## Fix

Add `"packageRules": [{ "matchManagers": ["github-actions", "pre-commit"], "semanticCommitType": "chore", "semanticCommitScope": "actions" }]`.

## Resolution
Added packageRules to .github/renovate.json giving github-actions and pre-commit updates semanticCommitType chore, scope actions.
title: Renovate CI-only major bumps are labelled chore(deps)! and would cut a major release

body:
## Problem

`pre-commit run --all-files` on a clean `main` exits 1. The `pretty-format-json` hook (`.pre-commit-config.yaml:22-23`) rewrites `.github/renovate.json` and `.releaserc.json` (expanding arrays one element per line), which Prettier — the JSON formatter MegaLinter runs in CI — collapses back. The config also carries hooks for file types this repo does not have (`requirements-txt-fixer`, `check-toml`, `check-xml`).

## Evidence

```text
$ pre-commit run --all-files
pretty format json.......Failed
- hook id: pretty-format-json
- files were modified by this hook      (.github/renovate.json, .releaserc.json)
```

`base-configs-commitlint/.pre-commit-config.yaml` removed the hook for this reason: "Two autofixers reverting each other fail every run."

## Impact

Contributors who install the hooks cannot commit JSON without a reformat loop, and the hooks cannot be used as a CI gate.

## Fix

Delete the `pretty-format-json`, `requirements-txt-fixer`, `check-toml` and `check-xml` hooks; let Prettier own JSON formatting.

## Resolution
Removed pretty-format-json, requirements-txt-fixer, check-toml and check-xml from .pre-commit-config.yaml. `pre-commit run --all-files` now exits 0 with no files modified.
title: pre-commit --all-files fails on main: pretty-format-json fights Prettier

body:
## Problem

Integrity gap. `yarn.lock` has 26 entries with a `resolution` but no `checksum` — every `@rolldown/binding-*` 1.0.3 and `lightningcss-*` 1.32.0 platform package, including the ones CI actually installs (`@rolldown/binding-linux-x64-gnu`, `lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu`). Yarn records no checksum for conditional packages it did not fetch when writing the lock, so these are installed without integrity verification.

## Evidence

Parsed `yarn.lock`: 26 entries lacking `checksum:`, all carrying `conditions: os=… & cpu=…`, e.g. `@rolldown/binding-linux-x64-gnu@npm:1.0.3 | os=linux & cpu=x64 & libc=glibc`. All are dev-only (vitest's toolchain).

## Impact

A substituted native binary for these packages would install without a checksum mismatch; exposure is limited to dev/CI machines.

## Fix

Add `supportedArchitectures` to `.yarnrc.yml` listing the platforms you install on (at least `os: [linux, darwin]`, `cpu: [x64, arm64]`, `libc: [glibc, musl]`) and run `yarn install` so Yarn fetches and records checksums for them.

## Resolution
The finding's premise was wrong. Yarn 4 deliberately omits lockfile checksums for os/cpu-conditional packages: with supportedArchitectures covering linux/darwin x64/arm64 and `yarn install --refresh-lockfile`, the same 26 entries still have no checksum. There is no repository-level control, so this is Yarn behaviour, not a defect here; the .yarnrc.yml change was reverted.
title: 26 platform-conditional binaries are locked without checksums

body:
## Problem

Broken link. `README.md:68` defines `[contributing-link]: https://github.com/ivuorinen/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Evidence

`gh api repos/ivuorinen/.github/contents/CONTRIBUTING.md` → `Not Found (HTTP 404)`; the recursive tree of `ivuorinen/.github` has no path matching `contributing`.

## Impact

Contributors following the README land on a 404.

## Fix

Add `CONTRIBUTING.md` to `ivuorinen/.github`, or drop the "contribution guidelines" clause.

## Resolution
Dropped the contribution-guidelines clause and the dead ivuorinen/.github CONTRIBUTING.md link definition from README.md.
title: README contributing link points to a file that does not exist

body:
## Problem

Parsed-but-unread entry. `package.json:52` declares `"semantic-release": "semantic-release --ci"`, but no workflow or document runs it — `publish.yml` releases through `cycjimmy/semantic-release-action` — and `semantic-release` is not a declared dependency; its binary resolves only through the transitive `@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` devDependency.

## Evidence

`grep -rn semantic-release .github/workflows/ README.md` (excluding the action and the config package) → no hits; `package.json` declares `semantic-release` in neither `dependencies` nor `devDependencies`; `node_modules/.bin/semantic-release` exists only via the transitive tree.

## Impact

Someone running `yarn semantic-release` locally triggers a real release attempt from a workstation with whatever `semantic-release` the transitive tree happens to hoist.

## Fix

Delete the `semantic-release` script from `package.json` (no twin needed: `publish.yml` is the release path).

## Resolution
Owner chose (r)emove: deleted the unused `semantic-release` script from package.json.
title: The semantic-release script is never invoked and relies on an undeclared binary

body:
## Problem

Non-gating check. `test.yml` (Test), `pr-lint.yml` (PR Lint) and `codeql.yml` run on `pull_request`, but `main` is unprotected and has no rulesets, while `allow_auto_merge` is `true`.

## Evidence

```text
$ gh api repos/ivuorinen/base-configs-eslint/branches/main/protection   → Branch not protected
$ gh api repos/ivuorinen/base-configs-eslint/rules/branches/main        → []
$ gh api repos/ivuorinen/base-configs-eslint --jq .allow_auto_merge     → true
```

## Impact

A PR that fails `yarn test` — including an auto-merged bot PR — merges and is published on the next push (`publish.yml` re-runs the tests, but by then the broken commit is on `main`).

## Fix

Add a ruleset on `main` requiring `Test / Test` (or `Test`) and `PR Lint`; verify with `gh api repos/ivuorinen/base-configs-eslint/rules/branches/main`.

## Resolution
ruleset 'main checks' (24025418) added on 2026-09-26: PR Lint, Test; verified via rules/branches/main
title: No check is required on main and auto-merge is on, so test failures do not block merges (verified)

body:
## Problem

The non-releasing rule in `.github/renovate.json` matches only `"matchManagers": ["github-actions", "pre-commit"]`, and the major-prefix rule only `["pre-commit"]`. Renovate's `nvm` manager, which updates `.nvmrc`, matches neither. `.nvmrc` is not in `package.json` `files`, and the workflows read it only through `node-version-file`, so a Node bump there never reaches consumers. Renovate still titles it with the preset default scope `deps`.

## Evidence

- Shared preset `github>ivuorinen/renovate-config` sets `semanticCommitScope: "actions"` only for `matchManagers: ["github-actions"]`, and sets `commitMessagePrefix: "chore(deps)!: "` on every `major` update. Its `chore(actions): ` override for majors covers github-actions only.
- Shared release rules (`@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` 3.0.0 `index.cjs:11-13`): `chore(deps)` gives a patch, breaking `chore(deps)` gives a major, and `chore(actions)` gives no release.
- Observed: ivuorinen/base-configs#577 and ivuorinen/base-configs-commitlint#196 (branch `renovate/node-26.x`, which changes only `.nvmrc`). Renovate titled both `chore(deps): update node.js (…)`, including force-pushes made after the actions/devDependencies rule landed (#578 / #201). The maintainer renamed both to `chore(actions): …` by hand before merging (PR timeline `renamed` events by the maintainer).

## Impact

Unless someone retitles the PR, every Node minor or patch bump merges as `chore(deps)` and publishes a needless patch release. In config-checker, each release then fans out into Renovate bumps across every @ivuorinen package. A Node major (for example 26 → 28) arrives as `chore(deps)!:` and publishes a **major** release of the package, even though consumers see no change.

## Fix

Add `"nvm"` to both manager lists, and update the first rule's description so it names `.nvmrc` as well:

```json
"matchManagers": ["github-actions", "nvm", "pre-commit"],
…
"matchManagers": ["nvm", "pre-commit"],
"matchUpdateTypes": ["major"],
"commitMessagePrefix": "chore(actions): "
```

The better fix is to make the same change once in the shared `ivuorinen/renovate-config` preset, next to its github-actions major rule, so all nine repos pick it up.

## Resolution
Fixed in the shared preset, ivuorinen/renovate-config#114 (merged as 503bbff): nvm (.nvmrc) and pre-commit updates get the literal prefix "chore(tooling): " and devDependencies/require-dev get "chore(dev-deps): " for every update type, so none carries the global "chore(deps)!: " major marker; "actions" stays reserved for github-actions. @ivuorinen/semantic-release-config releases on the deps scope only, so tooling and dev-deps commits cut no release (checked through commit-analyzer). ivuorinen/base-configs-eslint#249 then removed every local scope, prefix and group rule from this repo's .github/renovate.json, which now only extends the shared preset.
title: Renovate .nvmrc (nvm manager) updates are titled chore(deps) and release the package

## Problem

dependency-vulnerability in the vitest toolchain and the semantic-release chain.

## Evidence

osv-scanner 2.7.0, trivy 0.76.0 `--include-dev-deps` and `yarn npm audit --recursive` agree: vite 8.0.16 (GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm, GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv, GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw, GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw, GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22; fixed 8.3.3 on the 8.x line), @vitest/mocker 4.1.11 (GHSA-qxg6-89mg-rqv8, GHSA-xp26-3454-mjgp; fixed 4.1.12), ip-address 10.7.2 (GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5; 10.7.4). Open PR #265 bumps vite to 8.3.5.

## Impact

The vite advisories cover its dev server, which `vitest run` starts; the scanners fail on the lockfile.

## Fix

Bump vitest within 4.x (`yarn up vitest@^4.1.12`, which pulls a fixed @vitest/mocker), `yarn up -R vite ip-address`, confirm osv-scanner exits 0. vitest 5 (PR #250) fails with `Cannot find package 'vite'` because vitest 5 makes vite a peer; adopting it needs `vite` declared as a devDependency.

## Resolution
fix/audit-2026-10 99ba6fc: lockfile re-resolved under the 3-day gate within existing ranges; vite 8.3.5, vitest/@vitest/mocker 4.1.12, ip-address 10.7.4; osv-scanner: No issues found; 25/25 tests on Node 20.19.0, 22.13.0, 24 and 26.
title: yarn.lock resolves vite 8.0.16, @vitest/mocker 4.1.11 and ip-address 10.7.2, all with advisories

## Problem

supply-chain. `.yarnrc.yml` sets no `npmMinimalAgeGate`; the one-day gate in force is Yarn 4's built-in default.

## Evidence

`yarn config --why npmMinimalAgeGate` → `Source: <default>`. opengrep 1.31.0 rule `yarn-missing-minimal-age-gate` fires on `.yarnrc.yml:1`.

## Impact

A Yarn default change would silently remove the install-time guard.

## Fix

Add `npmMinimalAgeGate: 3d`, matching the shared Renovate preset's 3-day `minimumReleaseAge`.

## Resolution
fix/audit-2026-10 68d682d: npmMinimalAgeGate: 3d declared in .yarnrc.yml.
title: The npm age gate is inherited from Yarn's default instead of being declared

## Problem

`.gitignore` ignores the whole `docs/` tree. The local findings store and `docs/audit/arch-profile.md` exist but are invisible to git.

## Evidence

`.gitignore:135` is `docs/*`. `git ls-files docs/audit | wc -l` → 0 here; 4-7 in each of the other eight repos, which committed their stores in the `chore(audit)` PRs (#588, #282, #205, #206, #233, #235, #201).

## Impact

Resolved findings and the architecture profile for this repo exist only on one machine; a fresh clone re-audits from nothing.

## Fix

Remove the `docs/*` line and commit `docs/audit/` in a `chore(audit)` PR, matching the other repos.

## Resolution
fix/audit-2026-10 a8b73cf: docs/* removed from .gitignore; the store and arch-profile are committed on the same branch.
title: docs/* is gitignored, so this repo's findings store is untracked while the other eight track theirs

body:
## Problem

`Install Dependencies` is gated on `cache-hit != 'true'` and runs plain `yarn install`. publish.yml calls this workflow (`uses: ./.github/workflows/test.yml`) as its pre-release gate.

## Evidence

test.yml:52-53: `if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'` / `run: yarn install`. Plain `yarn install` rewrites a drifted lockfile instead of failing; on a cache hit nothing is installed at all.

## Impact

Lockfile drift passes CI, and on a cache hit the suite can run against a node_modules that no longer matches the manifest.

## Fix

Run `yarn install --immutable --mode=skip-build` unconditionally (the stylelint and config-checker pattern).

## Resolution
fix/audit-2026-10 6933a6a: test.yml installs with --immutable --mode=skip-build on every run; actionlint and zizmor clean.
title: The test workflow, which also gates publishing, skips the install on a cache hit and never runs it with --immutable
